solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hedge, given question — tick Sue off

indicators.note: off here means out of order, so the letters of these two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone told to deal with a hedge and a question tells Sue off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick Sue off' reads as a reprimand, but 'off' is the anagram signal on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Quickset is hawthorn planted as cuttings to grow into a living hedge, so the word names that kind of hedge.

clue.text: Islander from south with a complaint

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
a moan is a grumble or complaint

explanation.surface: An island-dweller from the southern hemisphere comes with a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Samoa, a Pacific island nation, is an islander.

clue.text: Warning: old people

parts.note: men can stand for people in general

explanation.surface: A warning notice addressed to elderly folk.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a sign foretelling something, often a warning of trouble ahead.

clue.text: Cope, breaking one's high standards

indicators.note: the cope word breaks into the one's letters, splitting them apart

parts.note: one is I, so one's is I'S, i.e. the letters IS
to deal with something is to cope with it

explanation.surface: Coping with pressure is cracking someone's lofty principles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' puts DEAL between the I and S of one's.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles or standards of perfection one aims for, a plural noun matching high standards.

clue.text: It creates mist damaging to armies

indicators.note: damaging the words breaks them up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weapon that makes a fog harmful to armies, like a chemical attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' rearranges the letters of TO ARMIES.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a spray device turning liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: Aristocrat said to be unable to produce heir

indicators.note: said to be signals a word that sounds like the aristocrat's title when spoken

parts.note: a baron is a nobleman, an aristocrat

explanation.surface: A nobleman rumoured to be unable to father an heir.
explanation.definitionFit: Barren means infertile, so unable to produce offspring such as an heir.

clue.text: Animal found in salt water loch

parts.note: the sea is a body of salt water
L is a map abbreviation for loch or lake

explanation.surface: A creature spotted in a briny Scottish loch.
explanation.definitionFit: A seal is a marine mammal, an animal of the sea and coasts.

clue.text: Maybe defenceless, but not hurt when husband leaves

indicators.note: the husband leaves, so his letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: unharmed means not hurt

explanation.surface: A wife left defenceless but unhurt once her husband walks out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' removes the H from UNHARMED. 'Maybe' marks the definition as one example: unarmed is one way to be defenceless.
explanation.definitionFit: Unarmed means carrying no weapons, one form of being without defence.

clue.text: Discover whereabouts? Time to run

parts.note: to race is to run fast

explanation.surface: Having found where something is, it is time to rush off.
explanation.definitionFit: To trace someone is to track them down and locate where they are.

clue.text: Exult with new royal symbol

parts.note: to crow is to boast or exult

explanation.surface: Someone gloating over a freshly unveiled emblem of monarchy.
explanation.definitionFit: A crown is the headdress worn by a monarch and the emblem of royal authority.

clue.text: Briefly wonder at a Liberal naval officer

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the wonder word goes

parts.note: to admire, in the old sense, is to wonder at

explanation.surface: Someone marvels for a moment at a Liberal politician who is also a senior sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the final E of ADMIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: An admiral is a flag officer of the highest rank in a navy.

clue.text: Putting together academic paper on moral offence, we hear

indicators.note: on means the paper is placed after the offence word
we hear means the word for moral offence is spoken and a word sounding like it is used

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence
a thesis is a dissertation, an academic paper

explanation.surface: A scholarly essay is being written about a wrongdoing, rumour has it.
explanation.walkthrough: SYN is the spelling that sounds like SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synthesis is the combining of separate elements into a whole, a noun form of putting together.

clue.text: Printout not easy to reproduce?

parts.note: hard means difficult, not easy
to copy is to reproduce

explanation.surface: A puzzled query whether a printed page is tricky to duplicate.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard copy is a computer document output on paper, which is what a printout is.

clue.text: Pinch small quantity of spirits

definitions.meaning: to pinch is to squeeze sharply between finger and thumb
a small measure of whisky or other liquor, a dram

explanation.definitionFit: Nip means both to squeeze sharply and a small drink of spirits.

clue.text: With no rival, don't strain so much to see

definitions.text: don't strain so much to see
definitions.meaning: read as two words, an instruction to squint less hard

explanation.surface: Unmatched in sight, so there is no need to squint.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer: peer (look hard) plus less.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerless means unequalled, having no match or rival.

clue.text: Something for waiter — start to put it back

indicators.note: back means the letters are put in reverse order
the start to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A diner leaving a gratuity is told to begin by putting it back.
explanation.walkthrough: P plus IT gives PIT, which 'back' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A tip is a gratuity left for service, the thing a waiter hopes for.

clue.text: Reshuffled, a sport minister

indicators.note: reshuffled means mixed up again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a cabinet reshuffle, one minister gets the sport portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a government minister; the answer is a minister of religion.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastor is a Christian minister in charge of a congregation.

clue.text: Concerned with teaching story that can be made good

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a parable is a simple story told to teach a moral

explanation.surface: A moral tale about something that can be put right.
explanation.definitionFit: Reparable means capable of being repaired or restored, made good again.

clue.text: Area within locality: Buckingham, for example

indicators.note: within means the area letter goes inside the locality word

parts.note: a place is a locality or spot

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood guide naming Buckingham as an example district.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckingham Palace is the London residence of the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckingham Palace is one example of a royal palace.

clue.text: Needle chap over family

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the chap word sits above the family word

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
kin means family, relatives

explanation.surface: A man irritating his relatives, needling them.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodkin is a thick blunt needle used for threading tape or cord.

clue.text: Cats, for example, can be melodious

definitions.meaning: Cats is a stage show by Andrew Lloyd Webber, an example of a song-and-dance show

explanation.surface: Felines are tuneful, the clue claims.
explanation.definitionFit: Musical is both a noun for a stage show with songs, like Cats, and an adjective meaning tuneful.

clue.text: Crush tree under motorway

indicators.note: in a down clue, the tree word goes under the motorway letter

parts.note: M is the British road designation for a motorway, as in M1
an ash is a tree

explanation.surface: A tree crushed beneath a motorway being built.
explanation.definitionFit: To mash is to crush something into a soft pulp.

clue.text: Perfect example of memo deleted? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, so the answer sits inside them

explanation.surface: Asking whether a deleted memo is the ideal specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is an ideal example worth copying.

clue.text: Skirt the centre of island

parts.note: mid means the middle or centre

explanation.surface: Going around the middle of an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Skirt' looks like a verb meaning go around; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A midi is a skirt whose hem falls to mid-calf.

clue.text: This boat reversing would make puddles

indicators.note: reversing means the word for puddles is read backwards

parts.note: puddles are small pools of water

explanation.surface: A boat backing up through the water would leave puddles.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloop is a one-masted sailing vessel, a kind of boat.

clue.text: They are on course to hold clubs

definitions.text: They are on course to hold clubs

parts.words: They are on course to hold clubs
parts.note: people on a golf course whose job is carrying a player's clubs; the surface hints at being on track to host clubs

explanation.surface: People on their way to holding clubs, like hosts of societies.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf caddies are attendants who carry a golfer's bag of clubs around the course.
